question: The Planning Commission of India was replaced by NITI Aayog in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2015.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Planning Commission (set up in 1950) was replaced by the NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) through a Cabinet Resolution dated 1 January 2015. (नीति आयोग — योजना आयोग का स्थान लिया)

 

• NITI Aayog began functioning as the premier policy think tank of the Government of India, providing directional and policy inputs, in contrast to the Planning Commission's role of allocating funds to ministries and states.

 

• The Prime Minister is the ex-officio Chairperson of NITI Aayog, and it has a Governing Council comprising all State Chief Ministers and Lieutenant Governors of Union Territories.

 

• Unlike the Planning Commission, NITI Aayog does not have the power to impose policies on states or allocate funds; it acts as an advisory/knowledge and innovation hub, promoting cooperative and competitive federalism.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The first CEO of NITI Aayog was Sindhushree Khullar, and Arvind Panagariya was its first Vice-Chairperson.

 

• NITI Aayog released the multidimensional National Multidimensional Poverty Index and coordinates the Aspirational Districts Programme.

 

NOTE

 

• 2016 (Option 1): No major restructuring of NITI Aayog occurred in this year; NITI Aayog was already operational since January 2015.

 

• 2018 (Option 3): Not the year of replacement; by 2018 NITI Aayog had already been functioning for three years.

 

• 2017 (Option 4): Also not the year of replacement; this year is unrelated to the Planning Commission's abolition.

question: Who was the first female Muslim ruler of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Razia Sultan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Razia Sultan (also called Razia al-Din) became the ruler of the Delhi Sultanate in 1236 CE, making her the first and only female Muslim ruler of Delhi/India. (रज़िया सुल्तान — दिल्ली की पहली मुस्लिम महिला शासक)

 

• She was the daughter of Sultan Iltutmish of the Mamluk (Slave) dynasty, who nominated her as his successor over his sons, recognising her ability.

 

• She ruled for about four years (1236-1240 CE) before being overthrown and killed by rebellious nobles (the "Chalisa"/Chahalgani) who resented being ruled by a woman.

 

• She is noted for discarding the veil (purdah), dressing like a male ruler, and personally leading her army and administration.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Razia Sultan belonged to the Mamluk (Slave) dynasty, the first dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate, founded by Qutb-ud-din Aibak.

 

• After her, no woman ruled Delhi as sovereign until much later regional female rulers emerged in different parts of India.

 

NOTE

 

• Zebunnissa (Option 1): She was a Mughal princess, eldest daughter of Emperor Aurangzeb, known as a poet, not a ruler.

 

• Chand Bibi (Option 3): She was a regent/warrior queen of Ahmednagar and Bijapur in the late 16th century, famous for defending Ahmednagar against Mughal forces, but she ruled as a regent, not as the first female Muslim sovereign of Delhi.

 

• Jahanara (Option 4): She was the eldest daughter of Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan, an influential princess but never a ruler in her own right.

question: Who received a Nobel Peace Prize for dismantling apartheid in South Africa?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nelson Mandela.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Nelson Mandela was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1993, jointly with South African President F.W. de Klerk, "for their work for the peaceful termination of the apartheid regime." (नेल्सन मंडेला — रंगभेद उन्मूलन हेतु नोबेल शांति पुरस्कार)

 

• Mandela spent 27 years in prison (1962-1990) for his fight against the racially discriminatory apartheid system in South Africa before being released in 1990.

 

• He went on to become South Africa's first Black President in 1994, after the country's first fully democratic, multi-racial elections.

 

• His work with de Klerk to negotiate a peaceful end to apartheid and transition to democracy is what the 1993 Nobel Committee specifically honoured.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mandela's autobiography is titled "Long Walk to Freedom".

 

• He is often referred to by his clan name "Madiba" and is celebrated globally; 18 July, his birthday, is observed as Nelson Mandela International Day.

 

NOTE

 

• Rabindranath Tagore (Option 2): He won the 1913 Nobel Prize in Literature for *Gitanjali*, unrelated to apartheid or the Peace Prize.

 

• Mahatma Gandhi (Option 3): Despite being nominated multiple times, Gandhi never received the Nobel Peace Prize; he led India's freedom struggle through non-violence, not the anti-apartheid movement's culmination.

 

• Albert John Lutuli (Option 4): He was the first African Nobel Peace laureate, awarded in 1960 for his non-violent resistance to apartheid as ANC President, but the prize specifically cited for "dismantling"/ending the apartheid regime went to Mandela (with de Klerk) in 1993.

question: As of 2022, India is the ______ largest economy in the world (as measured by nominal GDP).
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fifth.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As of 2022, India became the 5th largest economy in the world by nominal GDP, overtaking the United Kingdom. (भारत — विश्व की 5वीं सबसे बड़ी अर्थव्यवस्था)

 

• The ranking (nominal GDP, 2022) stood as: 1. United States, 2. China, 3. Japan, 4. Germany, 5. India.

 

• This milestone was widely reported based on IMF World Economic Outlook data and reflects India's rapid post-pandemic economic recovery.

 

• India has since continued to grow and, going into 2025, further overtook Japan and Germany to become the 4th and then 3rd largest economy by some estimates -- but "as of 2022" the correct rank is Fifth.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's nominal GDP crossed the UK's GDP in 2022 partly due to the sharp depreciation of the British pound alongside India's strong growth.

 

• India is often cited as the fastest-growing major economy in the years following the COVID-19 pandemic.

 

NOTE

 

• Third (Option 1): India had not reached 3rd position as of 2022; it was 5th at that time.

 

• Second (Option 2): China holds the 2nd position by nominal GDP, far ahead of India in 2022.

 

• Fourth (Option 4): Germany held the 4th position as of 2022, just ahead of India.

question: Raman wants to use a rear-view mirror in his vehicle. Which type of mirror should he pick for it?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Convex Mirrors.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Convex mirrors are used as rear-view mirrors in vehicles because they always produce a virtual, erect, and diminished (smaller) image of objects behind the vehicle. (उत्तल दर्पण — वाहन का रियर-व्यू मिरर)

 

• Since the image formed is smaller than the actual object, a convex mirror covers a much wider field of view, allowing the driver to see a larger area of traffic behind and to the sides.

 

• This diverging nature of the mirror (it bulges outward) means the field of view does not depend on the distance of the object, unlike a plane mirror.

 

• A well-known caution written on such mirrors is: "Objects in the mirror are closer than they appear," because the diminished image can make trailing vehicles look farther away than they really are.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Convex mirrors are also used as security mirrors in shops and at blind road turns for the same wide-field-of-view property.

 

• Concave mirrors, in contrast, are used in shaving mirrors, torches, headlights and reflecting telescopes, as they can produce a magnified image.

 

NOTE

 

• Plane Mirrors (Option 2): Form an image of the same size as the object, giving a much narrower field of view -- unsuitable for wide-angle rear viewing.

 

• Cylinderical Mirrors (Option 3): Have curvature along only one axis and are not standard rear-view mirrors; they are used in specialised optical/anamorphic applications.

 

• Concave Mirrors (Option 4): Are converging mirrors that produce a magnified, sometimes inverted image at close range, making them unsuitable and even dangerous for judging distance in rear-view use.

question: When was the Direct Tax Code Bill introduced in the Parliament of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2010.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Direct Taxes Code (DTC) Bill, 2010 was introduced in the Lok Sabha in August 2010 by the then Finance Minister Pranab Mukherjee. (प्रत्यक्ष कर संहिता विधेयक — 2010)

 

• Its objective was to replace the archaic Income Tax Act, 1961, and the Wealth Tax Act, 1957, with a simplified, modern direct tax law.

 

• The Bill was referred to the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Finance and went through several revisions, but it eventually lapsed with the dissolution of the 15th Lok Sabha and was never enacted.

 

• Direct tax reform continued later through amendments to the existing Income Tax Act rather than a wholly new code.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• A Task Force on Direct Tax Code was later constituted in 2017 to review the income tax law and submitted its report in 2019, but no separate "Direct Tax Code Act" has been passed as of the exam date.

 

• "Direct taxes" include Income Tax and Corporate Tax, as opposed to "indirect taxes" like GST.

 

NOTE

 

• 2005 (Option 2): No Direct Tax Code Bill was introduced in this year; this was around the time of major indirect tax reforms like VAT implementation.

 

• 2020 (Option 3): By this year, the original DTC Bill had already lapsed; the 2017 Task Force report (submitted 2019) is a separate exercise.

 

• 2015 (Option 4): Not the year of introduction of the DTC Bill in Parliament.

question: Neeti wants to use an input device that works by sensing the user’s finger movement and downward pressure. Which among the following should she use?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Touchpad.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A touchpad (also called a trackpad) is a pointing input device that senses the position and downward pressure of a user's finger as it moves across a flat surface, used to control the on-screen cursor. (टचपैड — स्पर्श आधारित इनपुट यंत्र)

 

• It is commonly built into laptops as an alternative to a mouse, and can also register clicks/taps via pressure, similar to a mouse button.

 

• Touchpads work using capacitive sensing technology, detecting the electrical change caused by the finger's contact and movement.

 

• Because it directly senses finger movement and pressure, it precisely matches the description given in the question.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Touch-sensitive technology in touchpads is related to (but distinct from) the touchscreens used in smartphones and tablets.

 

• Other common pointing devices include the mouse, trackball, and joystick.

 

NOTE

 

• Scanner (Option 1): An input device that converts printed documents/images into digital form; it does not sense finger movement.

 

• Light pen (Option 3): A light-sensitive pointing device used to draw or select items directly on a CRT/compatible screen by detecting light, not finger pressure.

 

• Keyboard (Option 4): A text/character input device using keys, unrelated to sensing finger movement or pressure for pointing.

question: Which country hosted the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is India.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India hosted the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup 2022, held from 11 October to 30 October 2022. (फीफा अंडर-17 महिला विश्व कप 2022 — भारत में आयोजित)

 

• Matches were played across stadiums in Bhubaneswar, Goa, Guwahati, and Navi Mumbai.

 

• This was India's second FIFA tournament as host after successfully hosting the FIFA U-17 Men's World Cup in 2017.

 

• Spain won the title, defeating Colombia in the final.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The tournament mascot was named "Ibha", an Asiatic lioness, and the trophy tour covered several Indian cities before the event.

 

• India became the first country to host both the U-17 Men's and U-17 Women's FIFA World Cups.

 

NOTE

 

• Egypt (Option 1): Did not host this tournament; Egypt has hosted other continental football events (e.g., AFCON).

 

• China (Option 2): Was originally slated to host the FIFA Women's World Cup (senior) 2023 qualifying/Asian events in some years, but not this U-17 edition in 2022.

 

• France (Option 3): Has hosted major FIFA events like the FIFA Women's World Cup 2019, but not the 2022 U-17 Women's World Cup.

question: Which of the following is NOT an application software?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Operating systems.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Computer software is broadly divided into system software and application software. Operating systems (like Windows, Linux, macOS) fall under system software. (ऑपरेटिंग सिस्टम — सिस्टम सॉफ्टवेयर)

 

• System software manages and controls computer hardware and provides a platform on which application software can run.

 

• Application software, by contrast, is designed to help users perform specific tasks -- such as word processing, creating graphics, or managing spreadsheets.

 

• Since the question asks which is NOT an application software, the Operating System -- being system software -- is the correct choice.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other examples of system software include device drivers, utility programs, and language translators (compilers/interpreters).

 

• Popular application software includes MS Word, MS Excel, Adobe Photoshop, and web browsers.

 

NOTE

 

• Graphics software (Option 2): An application software (e.g., Photoshop, CorelDRAW) used for creating/editing images.

 

• Spreadsheet software (Option 3): An application software (e.g., MS Excel) used for tabular data and calculations.

 

• Word-processing software (Option 4): An application software (e.g., MS Word) used for creating and editing text documents.

question: Which among the following is another word for universe?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cosmos.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The word "Cosmos" is used as another term for the "Universe" -- referring to all of space, time, matter, and energy that exists, viewed as an orderly, harmonious system. (कॉसमॉस — ब्रह्मांड का पर्यायवाची)

 

• It comes from the Greek word "kosmos", meaning "order" or "the world," as opposed to "chaos."

 

• The study of the cosmos/universe as a whole -- its origin, evolution, and structure -- is called cosmology.

 

• The term is widely used in scientific and popular literature (e.g., Carl Sagan's famous book/documentary *Cosmos*) as a synonym for the universe.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The prevailing scientific model for the origin of the universe is the Big Bang Theory.

 

• Cosmology is the branch of astronomy/physics dealing with the origin and evolution of the universe.

 

NOTE

 

• Big Crunch (Option 1): A hypothetical scenario for the end of the universe, in which the universe stops expanding and collapses back in on itself -- it is a theoretical event, not a synonym for "universe."

 

• Astronomy (Option 2): The scientific study of celestial objects and phenomena -- a field of study, not a word meaning "universe."

 

• Supernova (Option 4): A powerful stellar explosion marking the death of a massive star -- an astronomical event, not a synonym for the universe.

question: “Pay Roll Automation for Disbursement of Monthly Allowances (PADMA)” was launched in June 2022 by Ministry of ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Defence.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Pay Roll Automation for Disbursement of Monthly Allowances (PADMA)" is a centralised, automated Pay & Allowances system launched for the Indian Coast Guard. (पीएडीएमए — रक्षा मंत्रालय की पहल)

 

• It was inaugurated on 28 June 2022 by Shri Rajnish Kumar, Controller General of Defence Accounts (CGDA), which functions under the Ministry of Defence.

 

• The system was designed to automate and streamline salary and allowance disbursement, reducing manual processing errors and delays for Coast Guard personnel.

 

• PADMA reflects the government's broader push toward digitisation of defence pay and accounting systems.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Controller General of Defence Accounts (CGDA) is the apex accounting authority for defence expenditure in India, headquartered in New Delhi.

 

• The Indian Coast Guard was established in 1978 and functions under the Ministry of Defence, tasked with maritime law enforcement and search-and-rescue.

 

NOTE

 

• Civil Aviation (Option 1): This ministry oversees air transport regulation (e.g., DGCA, airports) and was not behind the PADMA launch.

 

• Finance (Option 2): While the Finance Ministry oversees the national budget and taxation, PADMA was specifically launched under the Ministry of Defence's CGDA for Coast Guard pay administration.

 

• Culture (Option 4): This ministry deals with heritage, arts, and culture-related schemes and has no connection to PADMA.

question: Who among the following received the OSCAR for the best actor in leading role in 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Will Smith.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Will Smith won the Academy Award (Oscar) for Best Actor in a Leading Role at the 94th Academy Awards, held on 27 March 2022. (विल स्मिथ — सर्वश्रेष्ठ अभिनेता ऑस्कर 2022)

 

• He won for his portrayal of Richard Williams (father and coach of tennis stars Venus and Serena Williams) in the biographical film "King Richard."

 

• This ceremony became widely known for the on-stage incident involving Smith and presenter Chris Rock, which occurred just before Smith's award was announced.

 

• The Best Actress award that year went to Jessica Chastain for *The Eyes of Tashi Tsui*/*The Eyes of Tammy Faye*.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Best Picture award at the 94th Academy Awards went to "CODA."

 

• The Academy Awards (Oscars) are presented annually by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences (AMPAS).

 

NOTE

 

• Benedict Cumberbatch (Option 1): Was nominated for Best Actor for *The Power of the Dog* at the 94th Academy Awards but did not win.

 

• Andrew Garfield (Option 2): Was nominated for Best Actor for *Tick, Tick... Boom!* at the same ceremony but did not win.

 

• Denzel Washington (Option 3): Was also nominated for Best Actor for *The Tragedy of Macbeth* that year but did not win.

question: In which year was the Dowry Prohibition Act passed in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1961.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 was passed by the Parliament of India and received Presidential assent on 20 May 1961, coming into force on 1 July 1961. (दहेज प्रतिषेध अधिनियम — 1961)

 

• The Act prohibits the giving, taking, or demanding of dowry as a condition for marriage.

 

• It defines "dowry" broadly to include property or valuable security given directly or indirectly in connection with a marriage.

 

• The Act was later strengthened by amendments in 1984 and 1986, and provisions like Section 498A of the IPC and the Dowry Prohibition (Maintenance of Lists of Presents) Rules, 1985 were added to support enforcement.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Under the Act, giving or taking dowry is punishable with imprisonment of not less than five years and a fine.

 

• Section 304B of the IPC deals with "dowry death," relevant when a woman dies under suspicious circumstances within seven years of marriage due to dowry-related harassment.

 

NOTE

 

• 1973 (Option 1): Not the year of enactment; this year is unrelated to the Dowry Prohibition Act's passage.

 

• 1982 (Option 2): Not the year of enactment of the original Act.

 

• 1954 (Option 4): This year corresponds to the Special Marriage Act, 1954 (a law on civil marriage), not the Dowry Prohibition Act.

question: PV Sindhu, a famous badminton player of India, won _______ Open title in July 2022.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Singapore.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• PV Sindhu won the Singapore Open 2022 women's singles badminton title in July 2022. (पीवी सिंधु — सिंगापुर ओपन विजेता 2022)

 

• In the final, she defeated China's Wang Zhi Yi to clinch the title.

 

• This was a significant title on the BWF World Tour, adding to Sindhu's long list of international badminton achievements.

 

• Sindhu is a two-time Olympic medallist (Silver at Rio 2016, Bronze at Tokyo 2020) and a former World Champion (2019).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• PV Sindhu hails from Hyderabad, Telangana, and trains under coach Pullela Gopichand.

 

• She has also won titles such as the World Championships (2019 gold), Commonwealth Games gold (2018, 2022), and multiple Super Series/World Tour titles.

 

NOTE

 

• Thailand (Option 1): Sindhu has competed in Thailand Open editions in various years, but her July 2022 title win was at the Singapore Open, not the Thailand Open.

 

• India (Option 2): There is no "India Open" title win by Sindhu specifically dated to July 2022 matching this event.

 

• Denmark (Option 3): The Denmark Open is a separate BWF tournament (typically held later in the year); Sindhu's July 2022 win was in Singapore.

question: Who became the first athlete to win Gold in Yogasana at the 36th National Games, India in 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pooja Patel.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pooja Patel, representing Haryana, became the first athlete to win a Gold medal in Yogasana at the 36th National Games, held in Gujarat in 2022. (पूजा पटेल — योगासन में स्वर्ण पदक जीतने वाली प्रथम खिलाड़ी)

 

• Yogasana was included as a competitive/demonstration discipline for the first time at the National Games, marking its recognition as a formal sport in India.

 

• Haryana thereby also became the first state to win a gold medal in Yogasana at the National Games.

 

• The 36th National Games were held across multiple host cities in Gujarat, with Gujarat as the primary host state.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Yogasana has been officially recognised as a competitive sport by the government, with the National Yogasana Sports Federation promoting it, and it has since been included in events like the Khelo India Games.

 

• Gujarat topped the medal tally at the 36th National Games, followed by Services and Maharashtra.

 

NOTE

 

• Manisha Kumari (Option 2): Not associated with the first Yogasana gold at the 36th National Games; the correct athlete was Pooja Patel.

 

• Soham Swami (Option 3): Not the athlete credited with this achievement.

 

• Raja Gupta (Option 4): Not the athlete credited with this achievement.

question: In India, palm, coconut, keora, agar are the common trees of which of the following forests?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mangrove Forests.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mangrove forests (also called tidal or littoral forests) grow in coastal and deltaic regions that are influenced by tides, and common trees include palm, coconut, keora, and agar. (मैंग्रोव वन — तटीय/ज्वारीय वन)

 

• These forests thrive in saline, waterlogged soil and are well adapted with features like stilt/prop roots and pneumatophores (breathing roots) to survive in oxygen-poor mud.

 

• The Sundarbans delta (West Bengal), formed by the Ganga-Brahmaputra river system, hosts the world's largest mangrove forest and is famous for the Sundari tree (from which "Sundarbans" gets its name) along with keora and agar.

 

• Mangroves are also found in the deltas of the Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, and Kaveri rivers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Royal Bengal Tiger is a famous inhabitant of the Sundarbans mangrove forest.

 

• Mangroves act as a natural barrier against coastal erosion, cyclones, and tsunamis.

 

NOTE

 

• Tropical Evergreen Forests (Option 2): Found in areas with heavy rainfall (over 200 cm); common trees include rosewood, ebony, mahogany, not mangrove species.

 

• Tropical Deciduous Forests (Option 3): India's most widespread forest type, with trees like teak, sal, shisham, that shed leaves in a particular season -- unrelated to mangroves.

 

• Montane Forests (Option 4): Found in hilly/mountainous regions with altitudinal variation in vegetation (e.g., chir pine, deodar, oak) -- distinct from tidal mangrove forests.

question: In September 2022, who was appointed as the Attorney General of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is R Venkataramani.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• R. Venkataramani, a senior advocate, was appointed as the Attorney General for India, with the appointment notified by gazette on 28 September 2022. (आर. वेंकटरमणि — भारत के महान्यायवादी)

 

• He succeeded K.K. Venugopal, taking charge as the 16th Attorney General of India, effective 1 October 2022.

 

• The Attorney General of India is the highest law officer of the country, appointed by the President under Article 76 of the Constitution, and serves as the government's chief legal advisor.

 

• The Attorney General has the right to speak and take part in the proceedings of both Houses of Parliament (or joint sittings) without a right to vote.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Attorney General holds office at the pleasure of the President and can also engage in private legal practice, unlike a full-time government employee.

 

• Below the Attorney General, other law officers of the Union include the Solicitor General and Additional Solicitors General.

 

NOTE

 

• Mukul Rohtagi (Option 1): Served as Attorney General of India from 2014 to 2017, prior to K.K. Venugopal's tenure -- not the September 2022 appointee.

 

• Ram Jethmalani (Option 2): A renowned senior advocate and former Union Law Minister, but he never held the post of Attorney General of India.

 

• KK Venugopal (Option 4): Was the Attorney General from 2017 to September 2022 -- the predecessor whom R. Venkataramani succeeded, not the September 2022 appointee.

question: Which among the following lakes is also known as the "Srinagar’s Jewel"?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dal Lake, located in Srinagar, Jammu & Kashmir, is popularly known as the "Jewel in the crown of Kashmir" or "Srinagar's Jewel." (डल झील — श्रीनगर का आभूषण)

 

• It is famous for its houseboats (shikaras), floating gardens, and the surrounding Mughal gardens such as Shalimar Bagh and Nishat Bagh.

 

• Dal Lake is the second largest lake in Jammu & Kashmir and a major tourist attraction, integral to Srinagar's identity and economy.

 

• The lake is divided into four basins: Gagribal, Lokut Dal, Bod Dal, and Nagin, connected by channels.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Dal Lake is fed by the Telbal Nallah and other channels, and is an important part of Srinagar's urban wetland ecosystem.

 

• Srinagar's famous Mughal Gardens (Shalimar Bagh, Nishat Bagh, Chashme Shahi) are located along the banks of Dal Lake.

 

NOTE

 

• Tsomgo (Option 1): A glacial lake located in Sikkim, near the India-China border, popular for tourism but not related to Srinagar.

 

• Vembanad (Option 2): The longest lake in India, located in Kerala, famous for backwaters and houseboats, but unrelated to Srinagar.

 

• Loktak (Option 4): The largest freshwater lake in Northeast India, located in Manipur, known for its floating phumdis (islands), not associated with Srinagar.

question: Somewhat before the time of Mauryan empire, about ______ years ago, emperors in China began building the Great Wall.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2400.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• According to the standard NCERT Class 6 History textbook, emperors in China began building the Great Wall of China about 2,400 years ago, somewhat before the time of the Mauryan Empire in India. (चीन की महान दीवार — लगभग 2400 वर्ष पूर्व निर्माण प्रारंभ)

 

• The wall was built to protect Chinese territories from invasions and raids by nomadic tribes from the north.

 

• Its construction spanned centuries, with major sections built and later connected/reinforced during the Qin dynasty (under Emperor Qin Shi Huang) and further extended in later dynasties, notably the Ming dynasty.

 

• The Mauryan Empire in India was founded by Chandragupta Maurya around 321 BCE, placing the beginning of the Great Wall's construction slightly earlier in history.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Great Wall of China stretches over thousands of kilometres and is often (though somewhat inaccurately) cited as visible from space.

 

• It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, recognised as one of the most remarkable architectural feats in human history.

 

NOTE

 

• 1200 (Option 1): Understates the age of the Great Wall's origin relative to the Mauryan period as stated in the textbook.

 

• 3500 (Option 2): Overstates the timeline; this would place it well before the earliest phases of the Wall's construction.

 

• 600 (Option 4): Far too recent a figure and inconsistent with the historical timeline relative to the Mauryan Empire.

question: Shri Mani Prasad is associated with which form of music?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hindustani vocal music.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pandit Mani Prasad is a renowned Hindustani classical vocalist, associated with the Gwalior gharana of classical music. (मणि प्रसाद — हिंदुस्तानी शास्त्रीय गायन, ग्वालियर घराना)

 

• He trained under stalwarts of the Gwalior gharana, one of the oldest gharanas of Hindustani classical vocal music.

 

• He has been recognised with honours for his contribution to preserving and propagating the Gwalior gharana style of khyal singing.

 

• Hindustani classical music is the classical music tradition of North India, distinct from the Carnatic tradition of South India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Gwalior gharana is considered the oldest khyal gharana and has produced legendary vocalists such as Krishnarao Shankar Pandit and Omkarnath Thakur.

 

• Hindustani music styles include Dhrupad, Khyal, Thumri, and Tappa, whereas Carnatic music emphasises forms like Kriti and Varnam.

 

NOTE

 

• Fusion Music (Option 1): A genre blending different musical traditions/styles (e.g., Indian classical with Western); not Mani Prasad's primary association.

 

• Folk Music (Option 2): Traditional, regional music passed through oral tradition (e.g., Bhojpuri or Rajasthani folk); not Mani Prasad's genre.

 

• Carnatic vocal music (Option 3): The classical vocal tradition of South India, associated with artists like M.S. Subbulakshmi, distinct from Mani Prasad's Hindustani (North Indian) tradition.

question: Which among the following peaks is the highest peak of Jharkhand?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Parasnath.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Parasnath (Parsnath) Hill, located in the Giridih district of Jharkhand, is the highest peak of Jharkhand, with an elevation of about 1,350 metres. (पारसनाथ पर्वत — झारखंड की सबसे ऊँची चोटी)

 

• It is also known as Marang Buru by local tribal communities and is considered one of the most sacred Jain pilgrimage sites in India.

 

• Twenty of the twenty-four Jain Tirthankaras are believed to have attained moksha (nirvana) on this hill, making it a major centre of Jain pilgrimage (Shikharji/Sammed Shikharji).

 

• The hill lies within the Parasnath Wildlife Sanctuary, part of the Chhotanagpur Plateau region.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Jharkhand was carved out of Bihar in the year 2000 and is rich in mineral resources like coal and iron ore.

 

• The Jain temple complex at Parasnath Hill is known as Sammed Shikharji.

 

NOTE

 

• Kangto (Option 1): The highest peak of Arunachal Pradesh, located in the Himalayas, unrelated to Jharkhand.

 

• Girnar (Option 2): A hill and important pilgrimage site in Gujarat, sacred to both Jains and Hindus, but not in Jharkhand.

 

• Anamudi (Option 3): The highest peak in the Western Ghats and in South India, located in Kerala, not Jharkhand.

question: Which pass connects the Kullu Valley with the Lahaul and Spiti Valleys of Himachal Pradesh, India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rohtang Pass.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rohtang Pass, situated on the Pir Panjal range in Himachal Pradesh, connects the Kullu Valley with the Lahaul and Spiti valleys. (रोहतांग दर्रा — कुल्लू और लाहौल-स्पीति को जोड़ता है)

 

• It lies at an elevation of about 3,978 metres and serves as a key gateway on the Manali-Leh Highway.

 

• The name "Rohtang" is believed to mean "pile of corpses," reflecting the historically hazardous nature of crossing it in bad weather.

 

• The Atal Tunnel, inaugurated in 2020, now provides an all-weather alternative route beneath the Rohtang Pass, reducing travel time and bypassing snow closures.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rohtang Pass is a major tourist attraction near Manali, famous for snow activities, though access is regulated due to environmental sensitivity.

 

• The Atal Tunnel is one of the world's longest highway tunnels above 10,000 feet, built under the Rohtang Pass.

 

NOTE

 

• Banihal Pass (Option 1): Connects the Kashmir Valley with the Jammu region, located in Jammu & Kashmir, not Himachal Pradesh's Kullu-Lahaul route.

 

• Thamarassery Pass (Option 2): Located in Kerala, connecting the Malabar coast to Wayanad; unrelated to Himachal Pradesh.

 

• Lipulekh Pass (Option 4): A Himalayan pass connecting Uttarakhand (India) with Tibet (China), used for the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra, not connecting Kullu with Lahaul-Spiti.

question: Who among the following was the architect of the Integrated Guided Missile Development Program (IGMDP) in India?
option_3: <style> @font-face { font-family: 'Kalam'; src: url('https://static-appxdb-v2.akamai.net.in/fonts/Kalam.ttf') format('truetype');} </style>A. P. J. Abdul Kalam
solution_text:
The correct answer is A. P. J. Abdul Kalam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam was the chief architect of the Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme (IGMDP), launched in 1983 to achieve self-sufficiency in missile technology. (डॉ. ए.पी.जे. अब्दुल कलाम — मिसाइल मैन ऑफ इंडिया)

 

• Under IGMDP, India developed five major missiles: Prithvi, Agni, Trishul, Akash, and Nag.

 

• For his pivotal role, Kalam earned the title "Missile Man of India" and later served as the 11th President of India (2002-2007).

 

• He was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1997, India's highest civilian honour, for his contributions to science and technology.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Before IGMDP, Kalam had also worked on India's satellite launch vehicle (SLV-III) programme at ISRO.

 

• Kalam's autobiography, "Wings of Fire," details his journey and role in India's missile and space programmes.

 

NOTE

 

• Har Gobind Khorana (Option 1): A Nobel Prize-winning biochemist (1968, Physiology/Medicine) known for work on the genetic code, unrelated to missile development.

 

• Vikram Sarabhai (Option 2): Known as the "Father of the Indian Space Programme"; he founded ISRO but is not credited as the architect of IGMDP.

 

• Homi J. Bhabha (Option 4): Known as the "Father of the Indian Nuclear Programme"; he founded TIFR and the Atomic Energy Commission, unrelated to IGMDP.

question: Chikungunya is an infection caused by ______ mosquito.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Aedes.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chikungunya is a viral infection transmitted to humans by the bite of infected Aedes mosquitoes, mainly Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus. (चिकनगुनिया — एडीज मच्छर से फैलने वाला रोग)

 

• Symptoms typically include sudden high fever and severe joint pain, along with muscle pain, headache, nausea, fatigue, and rash.

 

• The same Aedes mosquito species are also responsible for transmitting other major diseases such as Dengue and Zika virus.

 

• Aedes mosquitoes are identifiable by their black and white striped legs and body, and they typically bite during the daytime.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Prevention of chikungunya focuses on vector control -- eliminating stagnant water where Aedes mosquitoes breed -- since no widely available specific antiviral treatment or vaccine was in routine use as of the exam period.

 

• The name "chikungunya" is derived from a word in the Kimakonde language, meaning "to become contorted," describing the stooped posture of patients due to joint pain.

 

NOTE

 

• Culex (Option 1): The mosquito genus responsible for transmitting Japanese Encephalitis, Filariasis (elephantiasis), and West Nile Virus, not chikungunya.

 

• Mansonia (Option 2): Also a vector for Filariasis (Brugia malayi), not chikungunya.

 

• Anopheles (Option 4): The mosquito genus responsible for transmitting Malaria, not chikungunya.

question: Aga Khan Palace is located in ______ city of Maharashtra.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pune.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Aga Khan Palace is located in Pune, Maharashtra, built by Sultan Muhammed Shah Aga Khan III in 1892. (आगा खान पैलेस — पुणे, महाराष्ट्र)

 

• It holds great historical importance as the place where Mahatma Gandhi, his wife Kasturba Gandhi, and his secretary Mahadev Desai were held captive by the British from 1942 to 1944 following the Quit India Movement.

 

• Both Kasturba Gandhi and Mahadev Desai died while imprisoned at this palace, and their memorials/samadhis are located within its premises.

 

• Gandhi himself donated the palace to the Government of India in 1972 as a tribute to Gandhian philosophy and the Indian freedom struggle; it now functions as a national memorial.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Aga Khan Palace is known for its Italian arches and sprawling gardens, and it now houses a memorial museum displaying photographs and artefacts related to Gandhi's life.

 

• It has also been recognised for its architectural blend of Indo-Saracenic style.

 

NOTE

 

• Aurangabad (Option 2): A city in Maharashtra famous for the Ajanta and Ellora Caves and the Bibi Ka Maqbara, not the Aga Khan Palace.

 

• Ahmednagar (Option 3): Known for the Ahmednagar Fort, where Jawaharlal Nehru and other leaders were imprisoned during the Quit India Movement, distinct from Aga Khan Palace in Pune.

 

• Mumbai (Option 4): Maharashtra's capital city and a major metropolis, but the Aga Khan Palace is located in Pune, not Mumbai.
